pages.title: Cross-Country Institutional Design
headings: Legal origin and investor protection as the design axis
What it cannot answer — the identification problem
pages.excerpt: Cross-country institutional design is the research strategy that exploits variation across national legal and institutional environments — investor-protection strength, legal origin, enforcement quality, and tax regimes — to identify how institutions shape corporate payout.…
pages.text: Cross-Country Institutional Design Cross-country institutional design is the research strategy that exploits variation across national legal and institutional environments — investor-protection strength, legal origin, enforcement quality, and tax regimes — to identify how institutions shape corporate payout. Rather than a single natural experiment within one jurisdiction, it treats the country itself as the unit of institutional variation, pooling firms from dozens of jurisdictions and asking whether payout tracks a ranking of minority-shareholder rights. The design's signature move is the interaction term: payout is regressed on firm fundamentals interacted with a country-level protection or legal-origin index, so that the coefficient reveals how institutions condition the payout decision. It is the methodological home of the agency theory of dividends — the entire outcome-versus-substitute debate was built and first tested on cross-country institutional variation. Its great strength, external validity spanning twenty to forty countries, is also its central weakness, because legal origin is correlated with countless omitted institutional and cultural traits, which is why the field has increasingly migrated toward the within-country regulatory shocks treated in natural-experiments-and-did-regulatory-shocks. This page sets out what the design does, how the legal-origin axis is operationalized, what it can and cannot answer, and where its inferential limits bite. What the method does The method pools firms drawn from many national environments and maps their payout behavior onto features of the country in which they operate, treating the country as the locus of institutional variation that firm-level studies within a single legal system cannot observe. The canonical implementation regresses payout measures for a cross-section of firms on firm controls and a country-level index of minority-shareholder rights, asking whether the institution shifts payout in the direction one theory predicts against another (laporta-2000-agency-problems-and-dividend-policies-around-the-world). The intellectual foundation is the legal-approach claim that the degree to which shareholders and creditors are protected by law from expropriation is the deep determinant of ownership concentration, capital-market development, and dividend policy — and that this legal lens explains cross-country differences better than the older bank-centered-versus-market-centered dichotomy (laporta-2000-investor-protection-and-corporate-governance). Later designs broaden the country descriptors layered onto the regression: tax systems interacted with protection (alzahrani-2012-investor-protection-taxation-and-dividends), and multi-country determinant studies that pit agency and lifecycle explanations against signaling and catering across a handful of developed economies (denis-2008-why-do-firms-pay-dividends-international-evidence-on). In every case the design's leverage comes from the same source: firms that are similar on fundamentals but sit in different institutional regimes reveal, through their payout differences, what the institution does. Legal origin and investor protection as the design axis The organizing regressor of the whole tradition is the legal-origin and investor-protection index — the common-law-versus-civil-law distinction and the anti-director-rights score that operationalize how strongly a country's law empowers minority shareholders. Turning this into a design axis means interacting a protection or legal-origin variable with firm characteristics, so that the sign of the interaction discriminates between competing theories: under the outcome model stronger rights predict higher payout, while under the substitute model they predict lower payout, and the cross-country test is precisely what adjudicates the two (laporta-2000-agency-problems-and-dividend-policies-around-the-world; laporta-2000-investor-protection-and-corporate-governance). The axis is not only a payout regressor; it also structures valuation and control-value studies. Catering behavior is present among firms in common-law countries but absent in civil-law countries even after controlling for lifecycle, a legal-origin interaction result showing that the institutional regime governs whether investors can force and price payout (ferris-2009-catering-effects-in-corporate-dividend-policy-the-international). And the legal environment — enforcement, investor protection, and takeover regulation — explains a large majority of the cross-country variation in the value of control-block votes, a template for how much institutional regressors can capture (nenova-2003-the-value-of-corporate-voting-rights-and-control). Cross-paper pattern: Across the LLSV-descended literature, the common-law/civil-law split behaves as the master institutional regressor: minority-rights strength maps onto payout, catering, and the private value of control, and the interaction of that index with firm characteristics is what turns a descriptive ranking into a testable design (laporta-2000-agency-problems-and-dividend-policies-around-the-world; ferris-2009-catering-effects-in-corporate-dividend-policy-the-international; nenova-2003-the-value-of-corporate-voting-rights-and-control). Standard implementation The workhorse specification is a pooled cross-country payout regression: a payout outcome (propensity to pay, payout ratio, or dividend yield) on firm-level controls — size, profitability, growth, leverage, the retained-earnings share of equity — plus country-level institutional variables entered directly and interacted with firm characteristics, typically with country or industry effects to soak up residual heterogeneity. Taxation is layered onto protection in the more refined designs: firms in strong-protection countries pay lower cash dividends than those in weak-protection countries under a classical tax system but repurchase more to maximize shareholders' after-tax returns, a result that requires jointly modeling protection and the tax regime rather than either alone (alzahrani-2012-investor-protection-taxation-and-dividends). Multi-country determinant designs add the lifecycle controls — size, profitability, and the earned/contributed capital mix — that let agency-lifecycle explanations be separated from signaling and catering (denis-2008-why-do-firms-pay-dividends-international-evidence-on). Valuation variants swap the payout outcome for firm value, regressing value on cash and dividends interacted with protection (pinkowitz-2006-does-the-contribution-of-corporate-cash-holdings-and), and some designs incorporate an insider-trading-law index as the country regressor of interest, testing payout, smoothing, and valuation against it across 24 countries (brockman-2014-the-impact-of-insider-trading-laws-on-dividend). What the design can answer The design answers questions about the institutional determinants of the payout level and its valuation that no single-country study can reach, because only cross-country variation supplies the institutional contrast. It can establish that the price investors attach to cash and to dividends depends on protection — the cash-value relation is much weaker where investor protection is poor, and the dividend-value relation is weaker where protection is strong, both consistent with agency theory (pinkowitz-2006-does-the-contribution-of-corporate-cash-holdings-and). It can characterize how firms in weak-institution countries commit to payout as a governance device: they exhibit a higher speed of adjustment to a target payout ratio, pay earlier in the lifecycle, and more often disclose a policy pledging a minimum share of earnings, revealing agency conflicts to future investors and easing external finance (ellahie-2021-show-me-the-money-dividend-policy-in-countries). It can measure how much of the cross-country dispersion in the private value of control is institutional rather than idiosyncratic (nenova-2003-the-value-of-corporate-voting-rights-and-control), and how tax regimes interact with protection to shift the cash-dividend-versus-repurchase mix (alzahrani-2012-investor-protection-taxation-and-dividends). It can also locate where a behavioral regularity like catering does and does not operate along the legal-origin divide (ferris-2009-catering-effects-in-corporate-dividend-policy-the-international). What it cannot answer — the identification problem The design's decisive limitation is that legal origin is not a clean treatment but a bundle of correlated omitted variables: a country's common-law or civil-law heritage travels with its enforcement quality, market development, disclosure norms, ownership structure, and culture, so a payout difference attributed to minority rights may instead reflect any of these co-moving traits. Cross-sections also cannot rule out reverse causality — payout norms and institutions may co-evolve — so the pooled regression identifies an association, not a causal effect, which is the central reason the field has turned toward staggered within-country shocks that hold the country fixed (glendening-2016-the-market-for-corporate-control-and-dividend-policies; chen-2020-corporate-governance-and-cash-holdings-evidence-from-worldwide). Two lines of evidence sharpen the worry from inside the cross-country tradition itself. A long-run study of all Belgian listed firms from 1838 to 2012 finds that dividend policy was remarkably stable and that changes in investor-protection and taxation legislation had little impact on it, which is hard to square with strong institutional determinism (moortgat-2017-investor-protection-taxation-and-dividend-policy-long-run). And a 29-country behavioral analysis shows that patience, loss aversion, and ambiguity aversion predict payout, implicating culture as a confounder that legal-origin indices may be silently absorbing (breuer-2014-the-behavioral-foundations-of-corporate-dividend-policy-a). Cross-paper pattern: The omitted-variable critique is now made from within the cross-country literature, not only against it — long-run within-country stability of payout despite legislative change (moortgat-2017-investor-protection-taxation-and-dividend-policy-long-run) and cross-country behavioral determinants (breuer-2014-the-behavioral-foundations-of-corporate-dividend-policy-a) both suggest that a legal-origin coefficient may be capturing culture, enforcement, or persistence rather than the letter of minority-rights law (denis-2008-why-do-firms-pay-dividends-international-evidence-on). Common pitfalls and refinements Beyond the omitted-variable problem, the recurring pitfalls are treating a legal-origin coefficient as structural, ignoring within-country persistence, and reading a cross-sectional interaction as if it were a policy experiment. The behavioral evidence is a direct caution: if mental-accounting traits such as patience and loss aversion shape payout across countries, then a specification that omits culture will load those effects onto whatever institutional index it does include (breuer-2014-the-behavioral-foundations-of-corporate-dividend-policy-a). The long-run Belgian evidence is a second caution against institutional determinism, showing that payout can be strikingly insensitive to the very legislative changes the cross-section treats as drivers (moortgat-2017-investor-protection-taxation-and-dividend-policy-long-run). The constructive response has been complementarity rather than abandonment: the cross-country design supplies the external-validity map — which relationships hold across many institutional regimes — while staggered within-country reforms supply the causal identification the pooled regression lacks, so board-reform DiD studies across dozens of countries are best read as the identification-strengthened successor to, not the rival of, the LLSV cross-section (chen-2020-corporate-governance-and-cash-holdings-evidence-from-worldwide; bae-2021-board-reforms-and-dividend-policy-international-evidence). The two designs are thus complements: the cross-section poses the institutional question at scale, and the within-country shock answers it credibly. Current assessment (2026-07): The field's center of gravity has shifted from pooled cross-country protection regressions toward staggered within-country regulatory shocks, precisely because legal origin cannot be cleanly separated from the institutional and cultural traits it travels with. The cross-country design retains a real role — it establishes external validity across regimes and frames the outcome-versus-substitute question at global scale — but a cross-sectional protection coefficient is now read as suggestive of an institutional relationship rather than as a causal estimate, with the causal weight carried by the DiD designs it motivated (bae-2021-board-reforms-and-dividend-policy-international-evidence; moortgat-2017-investor-protection-taxation-and-dividend-policy-long-run). pages.title: Dividend Announcement Event Studies
headings: Auxiliary tests layered onto the return
What it can and cannot answer
pages.excerpt: A dividend announcement event study measures the abnormal stock return in a short window around the public announcement of a dividend initiation, increase, decrease, or omission, treating the reaction as the market's revaluation of the firm attributable to the information the…
pages.text: Dividend Announcement Event Studies A dividend announcement event study measures the abnormal stock return in a short window around the public announcement of a dividend initiation, increase, decrease, or omission, treating the reaction as the market's revaluation of the firm attributable to the information the payout decision conveys. The design estimates a normal-return benchmark over an estimation window, computes cumulative abnormal returns (CARs) over the event window, and cross-sectionally relates those CARs to firm and announcement characteristics — the standardized dividend change, dividend yield, Tobin's Q, and the information environment — to discriminate among competing theories of what dividends mean. It is the workhorse research design behind virtually every empirical claim about the information content of dividends, and its estimates supply the raw material both dividend-signaling and agency-costs-of-free-cash-flow must explain. Its central limitation is that a return magnitude, however precisely measured, underdetermines the channel that produced it, which is why the design is routinely augmented with auxiliary tests and why its findings are read with attention to selection, drift, and secular change. This page treats the design; the interpretation of the results is handed to dividends-signaling-vs-free-cash-flow. What the method does The method infers information content from price movement: under semi-strong market efficiency, a statistically significant abnormal return in the announcement window implies the announcement revealed something the market did not already price. This inference is a joint hypothesis — a test of information content is simultaneously a test of the assumed model of normal returns and of market efficiency, so a non-zero CAR can never be attributed to information alone without maintaining those auxiliary assumptions. The design partitions naturally by event type, and the type matters for what can be learned. Regular dividend changes yield a signed, continuous surprise scaled by the standardized change and yield (denis-1994-the-information-content-of-dividend-changes-cash-flow); initiations and omissions are discrete, high-information events whose reactions are larger and asymmetric (michaely-1995-price-reactions-to-dividend-initiations-and-omissions-overreaction); and one-time distributions such as specially designated dividends and repurchases isolate a payout with weaker commitment, useful for separating cash-disgorgement from ongoing-signal interpretations (howe-1992-one-time-cash-flow-announcements-and-free-cash). Because each event type carries a different information structure, pooling them obscures the very cross-sectional variation the design exists to exploit. The direction of the surprise is defined relative to the market's prior expectation of the payout, so a maintained dividend can itself be informative — firms that hold the dividend unchanged in an environment of frequent revisions earn insignificant returns, a useful zero-benchmark against which increases and decreases are read (alyahyaee-2011-the-information-content-of-cash-dividend-announcements-in). The short window is the design's core defense: by confining measurement to a few days around a dated announcement, it minimizes the confounding drift and benchmark error that plague long-horizon return studies. Standard implementation The canonical implementation proceeds in three steps. First, a normal-return benchmark is estimated over a pre-event estimation window, most commonly the market model $$R{it} = \alpha_i + \beta_i R{mt} + \varepsilon{it},$$ though market-adjusted ($\alpha_i=0,\ \beta_i=1$) and characteristic-based benchmarks are also used. Second, the abnormal return on each event day is the realized return net of the fitted normal return, $$AR{it} = R{it} - (\hat\alpha_i + \hat\beta_i R{mt}),$$ and these are cumulated over the event window to form the CAR, $$CAR_i = \sum{t \in [\tau_1,\tau_2]} AR{it},$$ with long-horizon designs substituting buy-and-hold abnormal returns (BHARs). Third, the CARs are regressed cross-sectionally on announcement and firm characteristics. The canonical specification simultaneously controls for the standardized dividend change, dividend yield, and Tobin's Q, so that the marginal contribution of each can be read off the coefficients (denis-1994-the-information-content-of-dividend-changes-cash-flow). Across the core studies, the announcement CAR scales positively with the standardized dividend change and with dividend yield (denis-1994-the-information-content-of-dividend-changes-cash-flow; yoon-1995-signaling-investment-opportunities-and-dividend-announcements), the empirical signature that makes the reaction interpretable as a response to the size of the surprise rather than a fixed announcement premium. Bond-price event studies run the same machinery on debt to detect wealth redistribution across claimholders (dhillon-1994-the-effect-of-dividend-changes-on-stock-and). Two implementation choices carry most of the inferential weight. The first is window length: short windows of a few days around the declaration date maximize power and minimize contamination, and their brevity makes the estimate largely insensitive to the choice of normal-return model, whereas the multi-year windows used to detect drift are far more exposed to benchmark misspecification and the joint-hypothesis problem. The second is the cross-sectional partition: because theory discriminates on how the CAR varies rather than on its average, studies sort firms on Tobin's Q, cash flow, dividend yield, and information-environment proxies, and it is the sign and significance of the interaction — not the mean CAR — that adjudicates between signaling and agency readings (denis-1994-the-information-content-of-dividend-changes-cash-flow; officer-2011-overinvestment-corporate-governance-and-dividend-initiations). This is why event studies of the same fact routinely reach opposite theoretical conclusions from nearly identical return estimates: the disagreement lives in the partition, not the CAR. Auxiliary tests layered onto the return Because the CAR alone cannot say why prices moved, credible studies layer additional tests onto the return to identify the channel. Analyst-forecast-revision tests ask whether professional forecasters revise earnings expectations in the direction of the dividend change, evidence that the announcement carried earnings-relevant information (denis-1994-the-information-content-of-dividend-changes-cash-flow; yoon-1995-signaling-investment-opportunities-and-dividend-announcements). Capital-expenditure-response tests track investment in the years after the announcement to distinguish signaling (where increases are followed by higher capex) from overinvestment discipline (where they should be followed by lower capex); Yoon and Starks find capex moves with the dividend and that no investment-policy news is released at the announcement (yoon-1995-signaling-investment-opportunities-and-dividend-announcements). Post-event operating-performance tests examine whether accounting performance actually improves after the payout, a design that discriminates sharply for repurchases — improvement appears only in low-growth firms and via asset shrinkage (nohel-1998-share-repurchases-and-firm-performance-new-evidence-on) — and that, for dividend decreases and omissions, uses benchmarks based on past performance characteristics to show earnings barely change afterward (lie-2005-operating-performance-following-dividend-decreases-and-omissions). These auxiliary layers are what convert a bare reaction magnitude into a test of a specific theory. The Q-partitioned announcement return is the most consequential of them: sorting initiations on Tobin's Q and cash flow, the design asks whether low-Q, cash-rich firms — those with the most overinvestment potential — earn the largest reactions, a signature that separates the agency reading from the Q-independent reaction signaling predicts (officer-2011-overinvestment-corporate-governance-and-dividend-initiations). Because these auxiliary tests draw on data outside the announcement window — analyst forecasts, multi-year capex, accounting performance, governance metrics — they inherit their own measurement and benchmark problems, so a well-designed study reports the announcement CAR and its auxiliary tests as a package whose joint pattern, rather than any single coefficient, licenses a theoretical claim. Variants and extensions Several variants exploit sources of variation the basic design cannot. Cross-listing designs use firms subject to different information environments — foreign firms cross-listing as ADRs — to sharpen test power where within-U.S. variation in information asymmetry is too small to detect signaling (aggarwal-2012-information-environment-dividend-changes-and-signaling-evidence-from). Cross-market institutional settings serve the same end: Oman's zero-tax, low-transparency, concentrated-ownership environment provides a natural test of whether a dividend tax penalty is necessary for informativeness (alyahyaee-2011-the-information-content-of-cash-dividend-announcements-in). Bond-price event studies extend the return measurement to debt to identify wealth transfers between stockholders and bondholders (dhillon-1994-the-effect-of-dividend-changes-on-stock-and). Return-decomposition variants apply the Campbell (1991) framework to split the reaction into cash-flow news and discount-rate news, recovering information the raw CAR conflates — Michaely, Rossi, and Weber use it to show the reaction reflects cash-flow rather than discount-rate news and tracks volatility rather than level (michaely-2021-signaling-safety). Tax-regime designs replace the cross-section with cross-time variation in dividend tax rates, measuring the share-price response per dollar of dividends (the "bang-for-the-buck") to test signaling against dividend-preference theories (bernheim-1995-a-tax-based-test-of-the-dividend-signaling). What it can and cannot answer The design reliably measures the magnitude of the market's reaction and its cross-sectional variation with firm characteristics, and it does so with the short-window precision that makes announcement studies robust to most benchmark choices. What it cannot do by itself is identify the channel: a given CAR is consistent with signaling, agency-cost reduction, wealth redistribution, and risk revaluation at once, which is exactly why the auxiliary-test layering above is not optional. Nor can the return reveal whether fundamentals actually follow — announcement reactions occur whether or not future earnings materialize, and the classic finding that increases do not predict future earnings growth is invisible in the CAR itself (benartzi-1997-do-changes-in-dividends-signal-the-future-or). The return-decomposition variant makes this concrete: the raw CAR cannot distinguish cash-flow-level news from cash-flow-volatility news, and only a structural decomposition recovers the distinction (michaely-2021-signaling-safety). Finally, the joint-hypothesis problem is irreducible — an anomalous CAR may signal a mis-specified benchmark rather than genuine information, and post-event performance evidence can undercut the naive reading, as when negative reactions to omissions turn out to reflect contemporaneous poor performance and market over-pessimism rather than a rational forecast (lie-2005-operating-performance-following-dividend-decreases-and-omissions). Current assessment (2026-07): The event-study CAR is a reliable measurement of the reaction to a dividend announcement but a poor instrument for the cause of that reaction. Consensus practice therefore treats the announcement return as a first stage to be paired with analyst-revision, capex-response, post-event-performance, or return-decomposition tests before any theory is credited (denis-1994-the-information-content-of-dividend-changes-cash-flow; yoon-1995-signaling-investment-opportunities-and-dividend-announcements; michaely-2021-signaling-safety). Common pitfalls Several recurring hazards degrade naive implementations. Confounding events — most often an earnings announcement released near the dividend declaration — contaminate the window unless screened out, since the CAR cannot separate the two pieces of news. Post-announcement drift is a substantive violation of the efficiency assumption: prices continue to move in the direction of the announcement for up to a year, the drift is stronger and more robust after omissions than initiations, and it is distinct from and more pronounced than post-earnings-announcement drift, to the point that a trading rule exploiting it earns positive returns in 22 of 25 years (michaely-1995-price-reactions-to-dividend-initiations-and-omissions-overreaction). Selection bias in announcement timing is subtler: firms that announce on Fridays experience a reduced market response on any weekday and share unobserved characteristics, so the apparent "Friday inattention" effect disappears once selection is corrected (michaely-2016-are-friday-announcements-special-overcoming-selection-bias). Secular decline is a generalization hazard — announcement CARs have fallen since the mid-1970s and shrink with institutional holdings, so estimates from different eras are not comparable (amihud-2006-the-declining-information-content-of-dividend-announcements-and). Benchmark misspecification compounds all of these through the joint-hypothesis channel. Cross-paper pattern: The two most-cited threats to clean inference are post-announcement drift and selection bias, and both were surfaced by the same research group across two decades — drift distinct from post-earnings drift (michaely-1995-price-reactions-to-dividend-initiations-and-omissions-overreaction) and a Friday "inattention" effect that is really a selection artifact (michaely-2016-are-friday-announcements-special-overcoming-selection-bias). The methodological lesson is that apparent behavioral anomalies in announcement returns frequently survive only until the sample-selection process is modeled explicitly. pages.title: Natural Experiments and Difference-in-Differences around Regulatory Shocks
headings: What it cannot answer, and common pitfalls
pages.excerpt: Natural experiments and difference-in-differences (DiD) estimation around regulatory shocks are the identification strategy by which payout research moves from correlation to causation. The design exploits a legal or regulatory change that reaches some firms — or some…
pages.text: Natural Experiments and Difference-in-Differences around Regulatory Shocks Natural experiments and difference-in-differences (DiD) estimation around regulatory shocks are the identification strategy by which payout research moves from correlation to causation. The design exploits a legal or regulatory change that reaches some firms — or some jurisdictions — but not others, at a datable moment plausibly exogenous to firm payout policy, so that comparing treated and control units before and after the change isolates its effect. Staggered adoption across U.S. states or across countries provides the workhorse variant, letting the researcher difference out common time trends and time-invariant firm characteristics through firm and time fixed effects. The method matters because payout determinants — governance, taxes, information, ownership — are themselves endogenous to the forces that drive dividends, so cross-sectional regressions cannot establish causality; the natural experiment is the field's principal answer. A striking property of the design is that the same tool yields opposite-signed payout effects across shocks, which reflects the economics of the shocks rather than any flaw in the method. This page treats the design itself — its counterfactual logic, its sources of variation, its variants, and what it can and cannot answer — and defers the substantive findings to the mechanism and synthesis pages. What the design does The DiD design rests on a counterfactual: the change in payout that treated firms would have experienced absent the shock is imputed from the contemporaneous change among untreated firms. Estimation regresses a payout outcome on a treatment indicator interacted with a post-shock indicator, absorbing firm fixed effects (to net out stable cross-firm differences in payout propensity) and time fixed effects (to net out economy-wide trends), so the interaction coefficient carries the causal effect under the parallel-trends assumption — that treated and control payout would have moved together but for the shock. The board-reform literature is the textbook instance: a DiD analysis of board reforms across dozens of countries estimates the payout response to a governance change while differencing out global time trends, and reads a post-reform rise in dividends as the reform's causal effect (bae-2021-board-reforms-and-dividend-policy-international-evidence). The cash-holdings companion applies the same structure to a channel one step upstream, estimating that board reforms reduce cash and redirect it partly toward dividends and repurchases (chen-2020-corporate-governance-and-cash-holdings-evidence-from-worldwide). The information-shock design shares the logic while emphasizing timing: payout changes are attributed to the shock only because they occur around the event and only for treated units (hail-2014-dividend-payouts-and-information-shocks). Even a stakeholder-orientation study built on state constituency statutes follows the identical template, estimating the effect of a legal change on repurchases and dividends through a treated-versus-control comparison (ni-2020-stakeholder-orientation-and-corporate-payout-policy-insights-from). Sources of exogenous variation The credibility of the design depends entirely on finding a shock plausibly unrelated to the payout policy it is used to explain, and the payout literature has assembled a rich menu of such shocks. Investor-protection and governance reforms supply one family: staggered passage of U.S. state securities-fraud ("blue sky") statutes (agrawal-2013-the-impact-of-investor-protection-law-on-corporate) and worldwide board reforms (bae-2021-board-reforms-and-dividend-policy-international-evidence; chen-2020-corporate-governance-and-cash-holdings-evidence-from-worldwide). The market for corporate control supplies another, through the staggered initiation of country-level merger-and-acquisition laws that raise the threat of takeover (glendening-2016-the-market-for-corporate-control-and-dividend-policies). Labor and stakeholder law supply a third: staggered state adoption of wrongful-discharge laws that raise firing costs (dang-2021-employment-protection-and-share-repurchases-evidence-from-wrongful) and state constituency statutes that let directors weigh non-shareholder interests (ni-2020-stakeholder-orientation-and-corporate-payout-policy-insights-from). Tax reforms provide sharp investor-level shocks — a Brazilian pension-fund tax reform (colombo-2018-the-role-of-taxes-and-the-interdependence-among) and a Swiss 2011 reform that let only some firms pay tax-exempt dividends (isakov-2021-what-if-dividends-were-tax-exempt-evidence-from). Direct payout regulation and share-structure reform round out the menu, from China's comply-or-explain dividend rule (he-2018-the-effects-of-a-comply-or-explain-dividend) to share-lockup expirations (fang-2017-trading-restrictions-and-firm-dividends-the-share-lockup) and the staggered legalization of share repurchases across countries (wang-2021-real-effects-of-share-repurchases-legalization-on-corporate). Cross-paper pattern: The same DiD design delivers opposite-signed payout effects depending on which shock it exploits — board reforms and blue-sky laws raise dividends (bae-2021-board-reforms-and-dividend-policy-international-evidence; agrawal-2013-the-impact-of-investor-protection-law-on-corporate), M&A laws and information shocks lower them (glendening-2016-the-market-for-corporate-control-and-dividend-policies; hail-2014-dividend-payouts-and-information-shocks), and employment-protection laws shift firms toward repurchases (dang-2021-employment-protection-and-share-repurchases-evidence-from-wrongful). The divergence is a property of the shocks, not the estimator. Staggered versus single-date designs Two structural variants recur. A single-date design turns on one dated national event that hits all treated units at once; a staggered design exploits a reform adopted by different states or countries at different times, so that early adopters serve as a control group for late adopters and vice versa. Staggering strengthens identification because it makes a single economy-wide confounder at the treatment date implausible — no common shock could line up with adoption dates that are spread over years — and it is the dominant form in the payout literature, appearing in staggered board reforms across 41 countries (chen-2020-corporate-governance-and-cash-holdings-evidence-from-worldwide; bae-2021-board-reforms-and-dividend-policy-international-evidence), staggered repurchase legalization from 1985 to 2010 (wang-2021-real-effects-of-share-repurchases-legalization-on-corporate), and staggered state wrongful-discharge adoption (dang-2021-employment-protection-and-share-repurchases-evidence-from-wrongful). The empirical signature the design must produce is that the effect appears only in treated units and only at the treatment date; a payout change that shows up in control units, or before adoption, undercuts the causal reading. Cross-paper pattern: The credibility of a staggered design rests on the treated-only-at-treatment-date signature — the effect materializes in the units subject to the change, at the moment of the change, and is absent among never-treated or not-yet-treated units (chen-2020-corporate-governance-and-cash-holdings-evidence-from-worldwide; hail-2014-dividend-payouts-and-information-shocks; dang-2021-employment-protection-and-share-repurchases-evidence-from-wrongful). What the design can answer Well-executed, the design recovers the direction and magnitude of a specific legal lever's effect on payout, and it does so with a credibility no cross-section can match. The board-reform estimate is a clean example: firms pay higher dividends after reforms, an outcome-model result whose causal status rests on the treated-versus-control timing (bae-2021-board-reforms-and-dividend-policy-international-evidence). The tax-reform designs deliver magnitudes — treated Swiss firms raised dividend payout by roughly 30% after gaining the ability to pay tax-exempt dividends (isakov-2021-what-if-dividends-were-tax-exempt-evidence-from). Just as important, the design supports heterogeneity tests that double as channel tests: interacting treatment with pre-shock characteristics shows where the effect concentrates, and matching that pattern to theory validates the mechanism. Board-reform dividends rise more for firms with weak pre-reform governance and in countries with strong external governance (bae-2021-board-reforms-and-dividend-policy-international-evidence); information-shock payout cuts are larger where agency issues are more severe (hail-2014-dividend-payouts-and-information-shocks); the Swiss payout response is weaker for firms prone to agency conflicts (isakov-2021-what-if-dividends-were-tax-exempt-evidence-from); and SOX-driven effects concentrate in overconfident-CEO firms while being absent among firms already compliant before the reform (banerjee-2015-restraining-overconfident-ceos-through-improved-governance-evidence-from). This "already-compliant control" trick — comparing firms the reform bound against firms it did not, because they already met the standard — is a recurring way to sharpen the counterfactual. What it cannot answer, and common pitfalls The design's assumptions are also its failure modes. Parallel trends can be violated if treated and control firms were already diverging; anticipation can contaminate estimates if firms adjust payout before a foreseeable reform, as with dividends timed ahead of an expected tax increase (buchanan-2017-uncertainty-and-firm-dividend-policy-a-natural-experiment). Confounding contemporaneous reforms are a serious threat when the "shock" is really a bundle: the Sarbanes-Oxley natural experiment combines the statute with concurrent NYSE/NASDAQ listing-rule changes, so any estimate reflects the package rather than one provision (banerjee-2015-restraining-overconfident-ceos-through-improved-governance-evidence-from). General-equilibrium spillovers can violate the assumption that controls are untreated: in the Brazilian tax reform, control firms also increased tax-deductible dividends — probably to attract institutional investors — so the naive DiD understates the treatment effect through control-group contamination (colombo-2018-the-role-of-taxes-and-the-interdependence-among). Finally, external validity is bounded — a result estimated off one jurisdiction's statute need not travel, and a single dated event offers no staggering to guard against a coincident macro shock (hail-2014-dividend-payouts-and-information-shocks). Current assessment (2026-07): The payout literature's shock-based designs are as credible as their weakest identification assumption, and two lessons now dominate practice. First, control-group contamination is a live threat rather than a textbook footnote — the Brazilian reform shows untreated firms responding to the same policy environment, so a clean never-treated control cannot be assumed (colombo-2018-the-role-of-taxes-and-the-interdependence-among). Second, staggered adoption is the field's default because it defeats single-date confounders, but it inherits the well-known fragilities of two-way fixed-effects estimation when treatment effects are heterogeneous across cohorts; the safeguard is explicit attention to timing, pre-trends, and cohort composition rather than a single pooled coefficient. Robustness practice Because the assumptions are strong, credible papers pair the headline DiD with a battery of validation. Falsification and placebo tests check that no "effect" appears where none should; propensity-score-matched control groups guard against treated and control firms differing on observables; and alternative treatment definitions confirm the result is not an artifact of coding. The Brazilian tax study is the exemplar, reporting that its results survive falsification tests and an alternative control group built by propensity-score matching (colombo-2018-the-role-of-taxes-and-the-interdependence-among). The share-lockup study checks robustness to alternative definitions of nontradable shares and to firm fixed effects and omitted time-varying characteristics (fang-2017-trading-restrictions-and-firm-dividends-the-share-lockup). Validation against theory-predicted heterogeneity is itself a robustness device — a treatment effect that concentrates exactly where theory says it should, as with board-reform effects in weak-governance firms, is harder to attribute to a spurious confounder (chen-2020-corporate-governance-and-cash-holdings-evidence-from-worldwide; bae-2021-board-reforms-and-dividend-policy-international-evidence). The cumulative standard is that a payout effect is believed only when it survives placebo tests, matched controls, and a heterogeneity pattern consistent with the proposed mechanism. pages.title: Do firms understate stock option-based compensation expense disclosed under SFAS 123?
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — Focusing on the four key option pricing model inputs-expected option life, expected stock price volatility, expected dividend yield, and the risk-free interest rate for the expected life of the option-this study finds that firms understate option value estimates…
pages.text: Do firms understate stock option-based compensation expense disclosed under SFAS 123? (2006) Paper claim — Focusing on the four key option pricing model inputs-expected option life, expected stock price volatility, expected dividend yield, and the risk-free interest rate for the expected life of the option-this study finds that firms understate option value estimates and, thus, stock-based compensation expense disclosed under SFAS 123. Raw markdown: aboody-2006-do-firms-understate-stock-option-based-compensation-expense Bibliographic Record Authors: Aboody, D, Barth, ME, Kasznik, R Journal: REVIEW OF ACCOUNTING STUDIES Year: 2006 DOI: 10.1007/s11142-006-9013-0 Relevance score: 3.0分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(governance)；股利政策(dividend) Abstract Focusing on the four key option pricing model inputs-expected option life, expected stock price volatility, expected dividend yield, and the risk-free interest rate for the expected life of the option-this study finds that firms understate option value estimates and, thus, stock-based compensation expense disclosed under SFAS 123. As predicted based on incentives and opportunities for management to understate SFAS 123 expense, the understatement of option value estimates is increasing in proxies for the magnitude of the expense, is greater for firms with weaker corporate governance, and, to a lesser extent, is increasing in the excessiveness of executive pay. The findings are strongest for the expected option life and expected stock price volatility input assumptions, consistent with firms' greater latitude in determining these inputs. We find weaker evidence of understatement associated with the expected dividend yield assumption, and none for the interest rate assumption, consistent with these inputs being less amenable to discretion. Taken together, our findings raise some concern that the exercise of management discretion adversely affects the overall reliability of SFAS 123 expense. 摘要（中文） 本研究聚焦于期权定价模型的四个关键输入——预期期权存续期、预期股价波动率、预期股利收益率，以及对应期权预期存续期的无风险利率——发现企业低估了期权价值估计，从而低估了依据SFAS 123披露的基于股票的薪酬费用。正如基于管理层低估SFAS 123费用的激励和机会所作的预测，期权价值估计的低估程度随该费用量级的代理变量增大而增大，在公司治理较弱的企业中更大，并且在较小程度上随高管薪酬的过度程度增大而增大。这些发现对于预期期权存续期和预期股价波动率这两个输入假设最为显著，这与企业在确定这些输入时拥有更大的裁量余地相一致。我们发现与预期股利收益率假设相关的低估证据较弱，而与利率假设相关的低估证据则不存在，这与这两个输入较不易受裁量影响相一致。综合来看，我们的发现引发了一些担忧，即管理层裁量权的行使对SFAS 123费用的整体可靠性产生了不利影响。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.title: Executive stock-based compensation and firms' cash payout: the role of shareholders' tax-related payout preferences
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — We hypothesize that the structure of executive stock-based compensation helps to align managers' payout choices with shareholders' tax-related payout preferences. Raw markdown: aboody-2008-executive-stock-based-compensation-and-firms-cash-payout Bibliographic…
pages.text: Executive stock-based compensation and firms' cash payout: the role of shareholders' tax-related payout preferences (2008) Paper claim — We hypothesize that the structure of executive stock-based compensation helps to align managers' payout choices with shareholders' tax-related payout preferences. Raw markdown: aboody-2008-executive-stock-based-compensation-and-firms-cash-payout Bibliographic Record Authors: Aboody, D, Kasznik, R Journal: REVIEW OF ACCOUNTING STUDIES Year: 2008 DOI: 10.1007/s11142-008-9068-1 Relevance score: 4.0分 Matched themes: 股利政策(dividend, payout) Abstract We hypothesize that the structure of executive stock-based compensation helps to align managers' payout choices with shareholders' tax-related payout preferences. Specifically, stock options, which are not dividend-protected, can deter self-interested executives from using dividends as a form of payout. In contrast, restricted stock, which is dividend-protected, is more likely to induce the use of dividends. Relatedly, shareholders' preferences for dividends, which are taxed as ordinary income, can depend on the income tax consequences of dividends relative to those of long-term capital gains. To test our hypothesis, we investigate whether the exogenous changes in shareholders' tax-related payout preferences following the 2003 dividend tax rate reduction result in predictable shifts in executive stock-based compensation and in managers' payout choices. Consistent with our prediction, we find a positive relation between the increased use of dividends in firms' payouts and the increased (decreased) use of restricted stock (stock options) in executive compensation, particularly for firms with a greater percentage ownership by individual investors and with lower costs associated with modifying the structure of their compensation plans. Our investigation of the role of shareholders' tax-related payout preferences in the design of executive stock-based compensation extends the prior literature that has largely focused on the role of incentive contracts in inducing managerial effort, risk taking, and retention. 摘要（中文） 我们假设，高管股权型薪酬的结构有助于使管理者的派现选择与股东与税收相关的派现偏好保持一致。具体而言，不受股利保护的股票期权可以阻止追求自身利益的高管以股利作为派现形式。相比之下，受股利保护的限制性股票则更可能促使公司使用股利。与此相关，股东对按普通收入征税的股利的偏好，可能取决于股利相对于长期资本利得的所得税后果。为检验我们的假设，我们考察在2003年股利税率下调之后，股东与税收相关的派现偏好的外生变化，是否导致了高管股权型薪酬以及管理者派现选择的可预测转变。与我们的预测相一致，我们发现公司派现中股利使用的增加，与高管薪酬中限制性股票使用的增加（股票期权使用的减少）之间存在正向关系，对于个人投资者持股比例更高、且修改其薪酬计划结构相关成本更低的公司尤其如此。我们关于股东与税收相关的派现偏好在高管股权型薪酬设计中所起作用的研究，拓展了以往主要聚焦于激励合约在诱导管理层努力、风险承担和留任方面作用的文献。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.title: Dividend payouts: Evidence from US bank holding companies in the context of the financial crisis
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — We study dividend payouts of 462 U.S. Raw markdown: abreu-2013-dividend-payouts-evidence-from-us-bank-holding-companies Bibliographic Record Authors: Abreu, JF, Gulamhussen, MA Journal: JOURNAL OF CORPORATE FINANCE Year: 2013 DOI: 10.1016/j.jcorpfin.2013.04.001…
pages.text: Dividend payouts: Evidence from US bank holding companies in the context of the financial crisis (2013) Paper claim — We study dividend payouts of 462 U.S. Raw markdown: abreu-2013-dividend-payouts-evidence-from-us-bank-holding-companies Bibliographic Record Authors: Abreu, JF, Gulamhussen, MA Journal: JOURNAL OF CORPORATE FINANCE Year: 2013 DOI: 10.1016/j.jcorpfin.2013.04.001 Relevance score: 11.0分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(governance, policy, reform, regulat)；股利政策(dividend, payout)；影响机制(agency, signal) Abstract We study dividend payouts of 462 U.S. bank holding companies before and during the 2007-09 financial crisis. Fama and French (2001) characteristics (size, profitability and growth opportunities) explain dividend payouts before and during the financial crisis. The agency cost hypothesis explains dividend payouts before and during (more pronouncedly) the financial crisis. The signaling hypothesis explains dividend payouts during the financial crisis. Regulatory pressure was ineffective in limiting dividend payouts by undercapitalized banks before the financial crisis. Our findings have implications for corporate finance and governance theories, and also for the regulatory reforms that are being discussed among policymakers. (C) 2013 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved. 摘要（中文） 我们研究了462家美国银行控股公司在2007—2009年金融危机之前和期间的股利支付。法玛和弗伦奇（Fama and French，2001）的特征（规模、盈利能力和成长机会）能够解释金融危机之前和期间的股利支付。代理成本假说能够解释金融危机之前和期间（更为显著地）的股利支付。信号假说能够解释金融危机期间的股利支付。在金融危机之前，监管压力未能有效限制资本不足银行的股利支付。我们的发现对公司金融和治理理论、以及对政策制定者正在讨论的监管改革都具有启示意义。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.title: The Internal Governance of Firms
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — We develop a model of internal governance where the self-serving actions of top management are limited by the potential reaction of subordinates. Raw markdown: acharya-2011-the-internal-governance-of-firms Bibliographic Record Authors: Acharya, VV, Myers, SC,…
pages.text: The Internal Governance of Firms (2011) Paper claim — We develop a model of internal governance where the self-serving actions of top management are limited by the potential reaction of subordinates. Raw markdown: acharya-2011-the-internal-governance-of-firms Bibliographic Record Authors: Acharya, VV, Myers, SC, Rajan, RG Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCE Year: 2011 DOI: 10.1111/j.1540-6261.2011.01649.x Relevance score: 5.5分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(governance, policy)；股利政策(dividend)；影响机制(agency) Abstract We develop a model of internal governance where the self-serving actions of top management are limited by the potential reaction of subordinates. Internal governance can mitigate agency problems and ensure that firms have substantial value, even with little or no external governance by investors. External governance, even if crude and uninformed, can complement internal governance and improve efficiency. This leads to a theory of investment and dividend policy, in which dividends are paid by self-interested CEOs to maintain a balance between internal and external control. 摘要（中文） 我们建立了一个内部治理模型，其中高层管理者的自利行为受到下属潜在反应的制约。内部治理能够缓解代理问题，并确保企业拥有可观的价值，即使投资者提供的外部治理很少或没有。外部治理即使粗糙且不知情，也能补充内部治理并提高效率。这导致了一个投资和股利政策理论，其中股利由自利的CEO派发，以维持内部控制与外部控制之间的平衡。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.title: A Theory of Income Smoothing When Insiders Know More Than Outsiders
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — We develop a theory of income and payout smoothing by firms when insiders know more about income than outside shareholders, but property rights ensure that outsiders can enforce a fair payout. Raw markdown:…
pages.text: A Theory of Income Smoothing When Insiders Know More Than Outsiders (2015) Paper claim — We develop a theory of income and payout smoothing by firms when insiders know more about income than outside shareholders, but property rights ensure that outsiders can enforce a fair payout. Raw markdown: acharya-2015-a-theory-of-income-smoothing-when-insiders-know Bibliographic Record Authors: Acharya, VV, Lambrecht, BM Journal: REVIEW OF FINANCIAL STUDIES Year: 2015 DOI: 10.1093/rfs/hhv026 Relevance score: 3.0分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(enforce)；股利政策(payout) Abstract We develop a theory of income and payout smoothing by firms when insiders know more about income than outside shareholders, but property rights ensure that outsiders can enforce a fair payout. Insiders set payout to meet outsiders' expectations and underproduce to manage future expectations downward. The observed income and payout process are smooth and adjust partially and over time in response to economic shocks. The smaller the inside ownership, the more severe underproduction is, resulting in an "outside equity Laffer curve." 摘要（中文） 我们发展了一个关于公司平滑收益和支付的理论，其情境是内部人比外部股东更了解收益，但产权确保外部人能够强制实施公平的支付。内部人设定支付以满足外部人的预期，并通过减产来向下管理未来的预期。观察到的收益和支付过程是平滑的，并对经济冲击作出部分且随时间推移的调整。内部持股越小，减产就越严重，从而产生一条“外部股权拉弗曲线”。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.title: Bank Capital and Dividend Externalities
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — Dividend payouts erode equity capital and affect the relative value of claims on a bank. Raw markdown: acharya-2017-bank-capital-and-dividend-externalities Bibliographic Record Authors: Acharya, VV, Le, HT, Shin, HS Journal: REVIEW OF FINANCIAL STUDIES Year: 2017…
pages.text: Bank Capital and Dividend Externalities (2017) Paper claim — Dividend payouts erode equity capital and affect the relative value of claims on a bank. Raw markdown: acharya-2017-bank-capital-and-dividend-externalities Bibliographic Record Authors: Acharya, VV, Le, HT, Shin, HS Journal: REVIEW OF FINANCIAL STUDIES Year: 2017 DOI: 10.1093/rfs/hhw096 Relevance score: 5.0分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(policy)；股利政策(dividend, payout) Abstract Dividend payouts erode equity capital and affect the relative value of claims on a bank. Through this channel, when banks have contingent claims on each other, one bank's capital policy affects the equity value and risk of default for other banks. When such externalities are strong, bank capital becomes a public good, whereby the private equilibrium features excessive dividends and inefficient recapitalization relative to the efficient policy that maximizes total banking sector equity. We relate these implications to the observed bank behaviour during the crisis of 2007-2009. 摘要（中文） 股利派现会侵蚀股权资本并影响一家银行各项求偿权的相对价值。通过这一渠道，当银行相互之间持有或有求偿权（contingent claims）时，一家银行的资本政策会影响其他银行的股权价值和违约风险。当此类外部性很强时，银行资本便成为一种公共品，此时私人均衡相对于使整个银行部门股权最大化的有效政策而言，表现为过度派现和低效的资本重组。我们将这些含义与2007-2009年危机期间观察到的银行行为联系起来。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.title: Do Investors Suffer from Money Illusion? A Direct Test of the Modigliani-Cohn Hypothesis
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — We propose a direct test of the explanation by Modigliani and Cohn (MC) for the positive correlation between inflation and equity values-that it results from investors' money illusion. Raw markdown: acker-2013-do-investors-suffer-from-money-illusion-a-direct…
pages.text: Do Investors Suffer from Money Illusion? A Direct Test of the Modigliani-Cohn Hypothesis (2013) Paper claim — We propose a direct test of the explanation by Modigliani and Cohn (MC) for the positive correlation between inflation and equity values-that it results from investors' money illusion. Raw markdown: acker-2013-do-investors-suffer-from-money-illusion-a-direct Bibliographic Record Authors: Acker, D, Duck, NW Journal: REVIEW OF FINANCE Year: 2013 DOI: 10.1093/rof/rfs005 Relevance score: 3.5分 Matched themes: 股利政策(dividend)；影响机制(alternative) Abstract We propose a direct test of the explanation by Modigliani and Cohn (MC) for the positive correlation between inflation and equity values-that it results from investors' money illusion. This explanation, unlike its main rivals, suggests that because in inflationary periods dividends will, on average, be higher than expected, dividend announcements will trigger positive abnormal returns. These will be higher the higher the inflation, and the more levered the firm. The behavior of abnormal returns of US stocks on dividend-announcement days from 1955 to 2007 supports these predictions. We investigate alternative explanations of our results. None dominates MC's. 摘要（中文） 我们提出了一个对Modigliani和Cohn（MC）关于通胀与股权价值之间正相关关系的解释的直接检验——即该关系源于投资者的货币幻觉。这一解释与其主要竞争者不同，它表明由于在通胀时期股利平均而言将高于预期，股利公告将触发正向异常收益。通胀越高、公司杠杆越高，这些异常收益就越大。1955至2007年美国股票在股利公告日异常收益的行为支持了这些预测。我们考察了对我们结果的替代解释，没有一个能够压倒MC的解释。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.text: STOCK-PRICE VOLATILITY, ORDINARY DIVIDENDS, AND OTHER CASH FLOWS TO SHAREHOLDERS (1993) Paper claim — This paper shows that the results of variance-bound tests depend on how cash distributions to shareholders are measured. Raw markdown: ackert-1993-stock-price-volatility-ordinary-dividends-and-other-cash Bibliographic Record Authors: ACKERT, LF, SMITH, BF Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCE Year: 1993 DOI: 10.2307/2329033 Relevance score: 9.5分 Matched themes: 股利政策(cash dividend, distribution, dividend, share repurchase)；影响机制(cash flow) Abstract This paper shows that the results of variance-bound tests depend on how cash distributions to shareholders are measured. As in prior studies, we find apparent evidence of excess volatility when a narrow definition of cash flow (dividends only) is applied. However, we are unable to reject the hypothesis of market efficiency when the cash flow measure also includes share repurchases and takeover distributions in addition to ordinary cash dividends. 摘要（中文） 本文表明，方差界检验的结果取决于如何衡量对股东的现金分配。与以往研究一样，当采用狭义的现金流定义（仅股利）时，我们发现存在过度波动的表面证据。然而，当现金流度量除普通现金股利外还包括股份回购和接管分配时，我们无法拒绝市场有效性假说。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.title: Stock Price Booms and Expected Capital Gains
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — Investors' subjective capital gains expectations are a key element explaining stock price fluctuations. Raw markdown: adam-2017-stock-price-booms-and-expected-capital-gains Bibliographic Record Authors: Adam, K, Marcet, A, Beutel, J Journal: AMERICAN ECONOMIC…
pages.text: Stock Price Booms and Expected Capital Gains (2017) Paper claim — Investors' subjective capital gains expectations are a key element explaining stock price fluctuations. Raw markdown: adam-2017-stock-price-booms-and-expected-capital-gains Bibliographic Record Authors: Adam, K, Marcet, A, Beutel, J Journal: AMERICAN ECONOMIC REVIEW Year: 2017 DOI: 10.1257/aer.20140205 Relevance score: 3.0分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(standard)；股利政策(dividend) Abstract Investors' subjective capital gains expectations are a key element explaining stock price fluctuations. Survey measures of these expectations display excessive optimism (pessimism) at market peaks (troughs). We formally reject the hypothesis that this is compatible with rational expectations. We then incorporate subjective price beliefs with such properties into a standard asset-pricing model with rational agents (internal rationality). The model gives rise to boom-bust cycles that temporarily delink stock prices from fundamentals and quantitatively replicates many asset-pricing moments. In particular, it matches the observed strong positive correlation between the price dividend ratio and survey return expectations, which cannot be matched by rational expectations. (JEL D83, D84, G12, G14) 摘要（中文） 投资者主观的资本利得预期是解释股价波动的关键要素。这些预期的调查测度在市场顶部（底部）表现出过度乐观（悲观）。我们正式地拒绝了这与理性预期相容的假设。随后，我们将具有此类特性的主观价格信念纳入一个由理性主体构成的标准资产定价模型中（内部理性）。该模型产生了繁荣-萧条周期，使股价暂时脱离基本面，并在数量上复现了许多资产定价矩。特别是，它匹配了观测到的价格-股利比与调查收益预期之间的强正相关关系，而这是理性预期无法匹配的。（JEL D83, D84, G12, G14） Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. Synthesis pages citing this source draw on the abstract above.

pages.title: Peer influence on payout policies
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — Using a large sample of US public companies, we find robust evidence that firms' payout policies, i.e., dividends and share repurchases, are significantly influenced by the policies of their industry peers. Raw markdown:…
pages.text: Peer influence on payout policies (2018) Paper claim — Using a large sample of US public companies, we find robust evidence that firms' payout policies, i.e., dividends and share repurchases, are significantly influenced by the policies of their industry peers. Raw markdown: adhikari-2018-peer-influence-on-payout-policies Bibliographic Record Authors: Adhikari, BK, Agrawal, A Journal: JOURNAL OF CORPORATE FINANCE Year: 2018 DOI: 10.1016/j.jcorpfin.2017.12.010 Relevance score: 6.0分 Matched themes: 股利政策(dividend, payout, share repurchase) Abstract Using a large sample of US public companies, we find robust evidence that firms' payout policies, i.e., dividends and share repurchases, are significantly influenced by the policies of their industry peers. To overcome endogeneity problems, we employ instrumental variable techniques based on peers' stock price shocks. Peer influence on payouts is more pronounced among firms that face greater product market competition and operate in better information environments. With regards to dividends, firms, especially smaller and younger firms, are more sensitive to industry peers that are similar to them in size and age. However, mimicking repurchases is concentrated among large and mature firms only. Peer influence on dividends, compared to repurchases, seems more stable across firm and industry conditions. Overall, peer influence on dividends, and, to a less extent, on repurchases, is consistent with a rivalry-based theory of imitation, which posits that firms imitate peers' actions to maintain their competitive parity. (C) 2017 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved. 摘要（中文） 利用美国上市公司的大样本，我们发现有力证据表明，企业的支付政策（即股利与股份回购）显著受到其行业同侪政策的影响。为克服内生性问题，我们采用基于同侪股价冲击的工具变量方法。同侪对支付的影响在面临更激烈产品市场竞争以及处于更好信息环境中的企业中更为显著。就股利而言，企业尤其是规模较小和较年轻的企业，对在规模和年龄上与自身相似的行业同侪更为敏感。然而，模仿回购仅集中于大型和成熟企业。与回购相比，同侪对股利的影响在企业和行业状况间似乎更为稳定。总体而言，同侪对股利以及在较小程度上对回购的影响，与基于竞争的模仿理论相一致，该理论认为企业模仿同侪的行为以维持其竞争均势。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.title: Information Environment, Dividend Changes, and Signaling: Evidence from ADR Firms
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — While theory suggests that dividends can be an important credible signal for firm performance, prior studies have been unable to provide strong evidence of dividend signaling among publicly listed U. Raw markdown:…
pages.text: Information Environment, Dividend Changes, and Signaling: Evidence from ADR Firms (2012) Paper claim — While theory suggests that dividends can be an important credible signal for firm performance, prior studies have been unable to provide strong evidence of dividend signaling among publicly listed U. Raw markdown: aggarwal-2012-information-environment-dividend-changes-and-signaling-evidence-from Bibliographic Record Authors: Aggarwal, R, Cao, J, Chen, F Journal: CONTEMPORARY ACCOUNTING RESEARCH Year: 2012 DOI: 10.1111/j.1911-3846.2011.01101.x Relevance score: 5.0分 Matched themes: 股利政策(dividend)；影响机制(information asymmetry, signal) Abstract While theory suggests that dividends can be an important credible signal for firm performance, prior studies have been unable to provide strong evidence of dividend signaling among publicly listed U. S. companies. One potential explanation for this inconsistency between theory and empirical evidence is that the cross-sectional variation in information asymmetry across U. S. firms is insufficient to provide adequate test power. In this study, we revisit the link between dividend signaling and firms' information environment by examining the dividend behavior of foreign firms that cross-list on the U. S. stock market in the form of American Depository Receipts (ADRs). Our evidence suggests that ADR firms with poorer information environments have stronger incentives to adopt dividend increases as a credible signaling device. We also find that such firms experience an increase in one-year-ahead earnings and a decline in systematic risk following a dividend increase. Additional analysis shows that ADR firms have fewer other information channels compared to similar U. S. firms. Overall, we provide evidence consistent with the importance of dividend signaling, especially for firms with poorer information environments. 摘要（中文） 尽管理论认为股利可以成为公司业绩的一个重要且可信的信号，但先前的研究一直无法在美国公开上市公司中提供股利信号传递的有力证据。理论与实证证据之间这种不一致的一个潜在解释是，美国公司之间信息不对称的横截面差异不足以提供充分的检验效力。在本研究中，我们通过考察以美国存托凭证（ADR）形式在美国股票市场交叉上市的外国公司的股利行为，重新审视股利信号传递与公司信息环境之间的联系。我们的证据表明，信息环境较差的ADR公司有更强的动机采用增加股利作为一种可信的信号传递手段。我们还发现，此类公司在增加股利后，其未来一年的盈余上升，系统性风险下降。进一步分析表明，与相似的美国公司相比，ADR公司拥有的其他信息渠道更少。总体而言，我们提供的证据与股利信号传递的重要性相一致，尤其对于信息环境较差的公司而言。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.title: The impact of investor protection law on corporate policy and performance: Evidence from the blue sky laws
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — Recent studies have debated the impact of investor protection law on corporate behavior and value. Raw markdown: agrawal-2013-the-impact-of-investor-protection-law-on-corporate Bibliographic Record Authors: Agrawal, AK Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCIAL ECONOMICS Year:…
pages.text: The impact of investor protection law on corporate policy and performance: Evidence from the blue sky laws (2013) Paper claim — Recent studies have debated the impact of investor protection law on corporate behavior and value. Raw markdown: agrawal-2013-the-impact-of-investor-protection-law-on-corporate Bibliographic Record Authors: Agrawal, AK Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCIAL ECONOMICS Year: 2013 DOI: 10.1016/j.jfineco.2012.08.019 Relevance score: 5.0分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(investor protection, law, policy)；股利政策(dividend) Abstract Recent studies have debated the impact of investor protection law on corporate behavior and value. I exploit the staggered passage of state securities fraud statutes ("blue sky laws") in the United States to estimate the causal effects of investor protection law on firm financing decisions and investment activity. The statutes induce firms to increase dividends, issue equity, and grow in size. The laws also facilitate improvements in operating performance and market valuations. Overall, the evidence is strongly supportive of theoretical models that predict investor protection law has a significant impact on corporate policy and performance. (c) 2012 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved. 摘要（中文） 近期研究一直在争论投资者保护法对公司行为和价值的影响。我利用美国各州证券欺诈法规（"蓝天法"，blue sky laws）的错时（staggered）通过来估计投资者保护法对公司融资决策和投资活动的因果效应。这些法规促使公司增加股利、发行股权并扩大规模。这些法律还有助于改善经营绩效和市场估值。总体而言，证据强有力地支持了那些预测投资者保护法对公司政策和绩效有显著影响的理论模型。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.excerpt: Paper claim — We develop a unified theory of dynamic contracting and assortative matching to explain firm dynamics. Raw markdown: ai-2021-a-unified-model-of-firm-dynamics-with-limited Bibliographic Record Authors: Ai, HJ, Kiku, DN, Li, R, Tong, JC Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCE…
pages.text: A Unified Model of Firm Dynamics with Limited Commitment and Assortative Matching (2021) Paper claim — We develop a unified theory of dynamic contracting and assortative matching to explain firm dynamics. Raw markdown: ai-2021-a-unified-model-of-firm-dynamics-with-limited Bibliographic Record Authors: Ai, HJ, Kiku, DN, Li, R, Tong, JC Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCE Year: 2021 DOI: 10.1111/jofi.12980 Relevance score: 7.0分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(law)；股利政策(distribution, dividend, payout) Abstract We develop a unified theory of dynamic contracting and assortative matching to explain firm dynamics. In our model, neither firms nor managers can commit to arrangements that yield lower payoffs than their outside options, which are microfounded by the equilibrium conditions in a matching market. The model endogenously generates power laws in firm size and CEO compensation, and explains differences in their right tails. We also show that our model quantitatively accounts for many salient features of the time-series dynamics and the cross-sectional distribution of firm investment, dividend payout, and CEO compensation. 摘要（中文） 我们构建了一个将动态契约与匹配相结合的统一理论来解释企业动态。在我们的模型中，无论企业还是经理人都无法承诺接受收益低于其外部选择的安排，而这些外部选择由匹配市场中的均衡条件所内生给定。该模型内生地在企业规模和CEO薪酬中产生幂律，并解释了它们右尾的差异。我们还表明，我们的模型在数量上解释了企业投资、股利支付和CEO薪酬的时间序列动态以及横截面分布的许多显著特征。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.excerpt: Paper claim — We find that firms that regularly access public debt (bond) markets are more likely to pay a dividend and subsequently follow a dividend smoothing policy than firms that rely exclusively on private (bank) debt. Raw markdown:…
pages.text: Dividend smoothing and debt ratings (2006) Paper claim — We find that firms that regularly access public debt (bond) markets are more likely to pay a dividend and subsequently follow a dividend smoothing policy than firms that rely exclusively on private (bank) debt. Raw markdown: aivazian-2006-dividend-smoothing-and-debt-ratings Bibliographic Record Authors: Aivazian, VA, Booth, L, Cleary, S Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCIAL AND QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS Year: 2006 DOI: 10.1017/S0022109000002131 Relevance score: 3.0分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(policy)；股利政策(dividend) Abstract We find that firms that regularly access public debt (bond) markets are more likely to pay a dividend and subsequently follow a dividend smoothing policy than firms that rely exclusively on private (bank) debt. In particular, firms with bond ratings follow a traditional Lintner (1956) style dividend smoothing policy, where the influence of the prior dividend payment is very strong and the current dividend is relatively insensitive to current earnings. In contrast, firms without bond ratings flow through more of their earnings as dividends and display very little dividend smoothing behavior. In effect, they seem to follow a residual dividend policy. 摘要（中文） 我们发现，与那些完全依赖私人（银行）债务的公司相比，经常进入公开债务（债券）市场的公司更有可能支付股利，并随后遵循股利平滑政策。具体而言，拥有债券评级的公司遵循传统的Lintner（1956）式股利平滑政策，即前期股利支付的影响非常强，而当前股利对当前盈利相对不敏感。相比之下，没有债券评级的公司会将更多盈利以股利形式流出，几乎不表现出股利平滑行为。实际上，它们似乎遵循的是剩余股利政策。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.excerpt: Paper claim — While reports in the financial press suggest that share repurchases are harmful to bondholders, academic studies report conflicting empirical evidence. Raw markdown: alderson-2020-an-examination-of-the-wealth-effects-of-share Bibliographic Record Authors: Alderson,…
pages.text: An examination of the wealth effects of share repurchases on bondholders (2020) Paper claim — While reports in the financial press suggest that share repurchases are harmful to bondholders, academic studies report conflicting empirical evidence. Raw markdown: alderson-2020-an-examination-of-the-wealth-effects-of-share Bibliographic Record Authors: Alderson, MJ, Halford, JT, Sibilkov, V Journal: JOURNAL OF CORPORATE FINANCE Year: 2020 DOI: 10.1016/j.jcorpfin.2019.101499 Relevance score: 3.5分 Matched themes: 股利政策(share repurchase)；影响机制(expropri) Abstract While reports in the financial press suggest that share repurchases are harmful to bondholders, academic studies report conflicting empirical evidence. Using newly available daily bond data (versus monthly data used in existing studies) and modern methods of analysis, we find no evidence of bondholder wealth expropriation. Merton (1974) model estimates of changes in the value of debt during share repurchases and changes in credit ratings following share repurchases produce no evidence of bondholder wealth expropriation. Overall, we find no evidence that repurchases measurably harm bondholders, suggesting concerns raised in the financial press are unfounded. 摘要（中文） 尽管金融媒体的报道表明股份回购对债券持有人有害，但学术研究报告的经验证据相互矛盾。使用新近可得的日度债券数据（相对于现有研究所用的月度数据）以及现代分析方法，我们没有发现债券持有人财富被侵占的证据。Merton（1974）模型对股份回购期间债务价值变化的估计，以及股份回购之后信用评级的变化，都没有产生债券持有人财富被侵占的证据。总体而言，我们没有发现证据表明回购在可衡量的程度上损害了债券持有人，这表明金融媒体所提出的担忧是没有根据的。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.text: A theory of dividends based on tax clienteles (2000) Paper claim — This paper explains why some firms prefer to pay dividends rather than repurchase shares. Raw markdown: allen-2000-a-theory-of-dividends-based-on-tax-clienteles Bibliographic Record Authors: Allen, F, Bernardo, AE, Welch, I Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCE Year: 2000 DOI: 10.1111/0022-1082.00298 Relevance score: 3.0分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(institution)；股利政策(dividend) Abstract This paper explains why some firms prefer to pay dividends rather than repurchase shares. When institutional investors are relatively less taxed than individual investors, dividends induce "ownership clientele" effects. Firms paying dividends attract relatively more institutions, which have a relative advantage in detecting high firm quality and in ensuring firms are well managed. The theory is consistent with some documented regularities, specifically both the presence and stickiness of dividends, and offers novel empirical implications, e.g., a prediction that it; is the tax difference between institutions and retail investors that determines dividend payments, not the absolute tax payments. 摘要（中文） 本文解释了为何一些公司偏好支付股利而非回购股份。当机构投资者相对于个人投资者被征税较少时，股利诱发“所有权客户群”效应。支付股利的公司吸引相对更多的机构，这些机构在探测公司高质量以及确保公司得到良好管理方面具有相对优势。该理论与一些已记录的规律相一致，特别是股利的存在及其粘性，并提供了新颖的实证含义，例如预测决定股利支付的是机构与散户投资者之间的税收差异，而非绝对税收支付额。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.excerpt: Paper claim — We provide a theory of informal communication-cheap talk-between firms and capital markets that incorporates the role of agency conflicts between managers and shareholders. Raw markdown: almazan-2008-attracting-attention-cheap-managerial-talk-and-costly-market…
pages.text: Attracting Attention: Cheap Managerial Talk and Costly Market Monitoring (2008) Paper claim — We provide a theory of informal communication-cheap talk-between firms and capital markets that incorporates the role of agency conflicts between managers and shareholders. Raw markdown: almazan-2008-attracting-attention-cheap-managerial-talk-and-costly-market Bibliographic Record Authors: Almazan, A, Banerji, S, De Motta, A Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCE Year: 2008 DOI: 10.1111/j.1540-6261.2008.01361.x Relevance score: 6.5分 Matched themes: 监管/治理(disclosure, monitor, policy)；股利政策(dividend)；影响机制(agency) Abstract We provide a theory of informal communication-cheap talk-between firms and capital markets that incorporates the role of agency conflicts between managers and shareholders. The analysis suggests that a policy of discretionary disclosure that encourages managers to attract the market's attention when the firm is substantially undervalued can create shareholder value. The theory also relates the credibility of managerial announcements to the use of stock-based compensation, the presence of informed trading, and the liquidity of the stock. Our results are consistent with the existence of positive announcement effects produced by apparently innocuous corporate events (e.g., stock dividends, name changes). 摘要（中文） 我们提出了一个关于企业与资本市场之间非正式沟通（即闲聊，cheap talk）的理论，该理论纳入了管理者与股东之间代理冲突的作用。分析表明，一种鼓励管理者在企业被严重低估时吸引市场关注的自主披露政策能够创造股东价值。该理论还将管理层公告的可信度与股权薪酬的使用、知情交易的存在以及股票的流动性联系起来。我们的结果与一些看似无关紧要的公司事件（如股票股利、更名）产生正向公告效应的现象相一致。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.title: Financing Frictions and the Substitution between Internal and External Funds
pages.excerpt: Paper claim — Ample evidence points to a negative relation between internal funds (profitability) and the demand for external funds (debt issuance). Raw markdown: almeida-2010-financing-frictions-and-the-substitution-between-internal-and Bibliographic Record Authors: Almeida, H,…
pages.text: Financing Frictions and the Substitution between Internal and External Funds (2010) Paper claim — Ample evidence points to a negative relation between internal funds (profitability) and the demand for external funds (debt issuance). Raw markdown: almeida-2010-financing-frictions-and-the-substitution-between-internal-and Bibliographic Record Authors: Almeida, H, Campello, M Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCIAL AND QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS Year: 2010 DOI: 10.1017/S0022109010000177 Relevance score: 5.5分 Matched themes: 股利政策(dividend, payout)；影响机制(substitut) Abstract Ample evidence points to a negative relation between internal funds (profitability) and the demand for external funds (debt issuance). This relation has been interpreted as evidence supporting the pecking order theory. We show, however, that the negative effect of internal funds on the demand for external financing is concentrated among firms that are least likely to face high external financing costs (firms that distribute large amounts of dividends, that are large, and whose debt is rated). For firms on the other end of the spectrum (low payout, small, and unrated), external financing is insensitive to internal funds. These cross-firm differences hold separately for debt and equity, and they are magnified in the aftermath of macroeconomic movements that tighten financing constraints. We argue that the greater complementarity between internal funds and external financing for constrained firms is a consequence of the interdependence of their financing and investment decisions. 摘要（中文） 大量证据指向内部资金（盈利能力）与外部资金需求（债务发行）之间的负相关关系。这一关系被解读为支持啄食顺序理论的证据。然而，我们表明，内部资金对外部融资需求的负向影响集中于那些最不可能面临高外部融资成本的企业（派发大量股利、规模大且债务有评级的企业）。对于处于另一端的企业（低支付、规模小且无评级），外部融资对内部资金不敏感。这些企业间差异对债务和股权分别成立，且在收紧融资约束的宏观经济变动之后被放大。我们认为，对于受约束的企业，内部资金与外部融资之间更大的互补性，是其融资与投资决策相互依存的结果。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus. pages.text: How sensitive is investment to cash flow when financing is frictionless? (2003) Paper claim — I analyze the sensitivity of a firm's investment to its own cash flow in the benchmark case where financing is frictionless. Raw markdown: alti-2003-how-sensitive-is-investment-to-cash-flow-when Bibliographic Record Authors: Alti, A Journal: JOURNAL OF FINANCE Year: 2003 DOI: 10.1111/1540-6261.00542 Relevance score: 5.5分 Matched themes: 股利政策(dividend, payout)；影响机制(cash flow) Abstract I analyze the sensitivity of a firm's investment to its own cash flow in the benchmark case where financing is frictionless. This sensitivity has been proposed as a measure of financing constraints in earlier studies. I find that the investment-cash flow sensitivities that obtain in the frictionless benchmark are very similar, both in magnitude and in patterns they exhibit, to those observed in the data. In particular, the sensitivity is higher for firms with high growth rates and low dividend payout ratios. Tobin's q is shown to be a more noisy measure of near-term investment plans for these firms. 摘要（中文） 我分析了在融资无摩擦这一基准情形下企业投资对其自身现金流的敏感性。这一敏感性在早期研究中被提出作为财务约束的度量。我发现，在无摩擦基准下得到的投资对现金流敏感性，无论在量级上还是在其所呈现的模式上，都与数据中观察到的非常相似。特别是，对于增长率高且股利支付率低的企业，这一敏感性更高。托宾q被证明对这些企业而言是近期投资计划的一个更嘈杂的度量。 Notes Abstract-only record — no full text is available for this paper in the corpus.
